title: feat(ts-rag): add Node/Express RAG template w/ streaming + request correlation IDs
author: Dana Lo
body:
Summary: Adds the v1 TypeScript RAG quickstart template targeting Redwood Hosted API. The default implementation is a Node/Express service with (a) streaming chat responses, (b) request/tenant correlation IDs, (c) structured logs, and (d) a minimal ingestion + query flow using a pluggable vector store adapter (default: local Qdrant via Docker). This PR is intentionally opinionated to match the cross-template contract being established in ENG-2841.

Motivation: We’ve had a steady stream of onboarding issues where TS users copy snippets without timeouts/retries, lose correlation IDs across proxies, and can’t debug streaming disconnects. This template should get a new user to a working RAG endpoint in <15 minutes while emitting the right IDs/fields so Redwood Console traces and dashboards are useful.

What’s included: - packages/templates/rag-typescript/: new template package (Node/Express) - Streaming support for Redwood chat completions (SSE-style streaming to the client; upstream uses fetch + ReadableStream parsing) - Request correlation: accepts inbound x-request-id (or generates one) and returns it; also forwards x-request-id to Redwood API as a header; includes traceparent passthrough when present - Minimal RAG flow: /ingest (CLI + HTTP) to chunk + embed docs; /chat to retrieve topK chunks and answer with citations - Vector store adapter interface with default Qdrant implementation; docs include extension points - Safe defaults: AbortController-based upstream timeouts, bounded concurrency on ingestion, and basic 429 handling guidance (note: full standardized retry helper is tracked in ENG-2847) - Logging: pino JSON logs w/ request_id, tenant_id, route, model, status_code; avoids logging raw prompts/doc text by default

API surface: - GET /healthz: liveness - GET /readyz: readiness (checks vector store reachable) - POST /v1/chat: chat with retrieval (supports stream=true) - POST /v1/ingest: ingest documents (multipart or URL list) - CLI: pnpm ingest --path ./data --tenant demo

Notable implementation details: - Streaming: The server exposes an HTTP chunked response (text/event-stream). We forward Redwood upstream stream tokens to downstream clients while also emitting a final “summary” event containing token usage + model/route tags for correlation. If the client disconnects, we abort the upstream request. - Request IDs: middleware sets req.context.requestId and always includes it in logs + response header x-request-id. If the client provides x-request-id, we preserve it to improve multi-hop correlation (e.g., behind API gateways). - Headers: we pass through traceparent and baggage when present; we also set x-redwood-client=quickstart-ts-rag and x-redwood-template-version (from package.json) for attribution. - Env var contract: aligns with draft in ENG-2841 (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_MODEL, REDWOOD_EMBEDDING_MODEL, VECTORSTORE_URL, LOG_LEVEL, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS). Naming was reviewed for consistency with Python RAG template.

How to run (local): 1) cd packages/templates/rag-typescript 2) cp .env.example .env (set REDWOOD_API_KEY) 3) docker compose up -d (starts qdrant) 4) pnpm install && pnpm dev 5) pnpm ingest --path ./sample_docs 6) curl -N -H "content-type: application/json" -H "x-request-id: demo-req-123" localhost:3000/v1/chat -d '{"query":"What does Redwood Inference do?","tenant_id":"demo","stream":true}'

Docs included: - Template README with “Production shape” notes: timeouts, retries, rate limit handling, secrets, and logging hygiene - “Proxy notes” section: required headers for streaming via common reverse proxies; recommended idle timeouts - “Console debugging” section: how to search by request_id and which tags to expect

Screenshots/recordings: - Added a short asciinema-style text capture in README showing streaming output and x-request-id echo.

Breaking changes: None (new package only).

Follow-ups: - ENG-2847: swap ad-hoc 429/backoff notes for the shared SDK helper once merged - ENG-2845: add telemetry contract validations (metric names/trace attrs) to the TS template - ENG-2851: add k8s manifest for the TS service once the common baseline is finalized

Commit summary: 1) chore: scaffold rag-typescript template package 2) feat: express server w/ health checks + request id middleware 3) feat: qdrant adapter + basic retrieval query 4) feat: chat endpoint w/ Redwood API + streaming proxy 5) docs: local run + docker compose + proxy guidance 6) chore: lint/format + pnpm workspace wiring

Files/areas changed (high level): - packages/templates/rag-typescript/src/server.ts - packages/templates/rag-typescript/src/middleware/requestContext.ts - packages/templates/rag-typescript/src/redwood/client.ts - packages/templates/rag-typescript/src/redwood/streaming.ts - packages/templates/rag-typescript/src/rag/retriever.ts - packages/templates/rag-typescript/src/vectorstores/qdrant.ts - packages/templates/rag-typescript/docker-compose.yml - packages/templates/rag-typescript/README.md - pnpm-workspace.yaml / root tooling updates

Review notes: - Monica Patel: Requested we standardize on AbortController timeout behavior + ensure upstream abort on client disconnect. Addressed in commit 4 (added res.on('close') -> controller.abort()). - Logan Wright: Requested we always echo x-request-id and include it in every log line; also asked to avoid high-cardinality baggage logging. Addressed in commit 2 (response header) and commit 6 (baggage not logged; only request_id/tenant_id). - Marcus Lin: Requested we do not log raw user queries/doc chunks by default and add a note about secrets in .env + .gitignore. Addressed in commit 5 (logging guidance + explicit .env in .gitignore). - Wei Chen: Requested README copy changes to match docs-site tone (avoid “guarantees”), plus a clearer “Next.js alternative” section. Addressed in commit 5.

CI: - build (node 20) ✅ - lint ✅ - unit tests ✅ - template smoke: start server + /healthz + /readyz ✅ - docker compose validation ✅

Merge: Squash merged by Dana Lo after approvals from Monica Patel, Logan Wright, and Marcus Lin. Wei Chen approved docs changes.
